title: Latent operations, and why multiplying changes the picture
hook: A latent is just numbers, so you can add and multiply them. Why that does nothing to an empty latent, a little early in a run, and a lot at the end.

verified.claim: LatentMultiply is s1 * multiplier and works on the numbers on the wire.
process_latent_in is skipped for an all-zero latent.
Previews multiply by latent_rgb_factors, then apply (x + 1) / 2 and clip.
LatentInterpolate fails with batch 2 and 4 channels: The size of tensor a (4) must match the size of tensor b (2).
verified.ref: the node's execute on random tensors

verified.claim: common_upscale bilinear on 2x noise gives spread about 0.633, matching the lab's 0.632.
nm_latent_ops ran on a CPU; b_latent_gain passes validate_prompt.

unchecked: We did not render b_latent_gain for this lesson, so what a real VAE decoder does with a multiplied latent is not shown here. We show the linear preview map, and we expect a real decoder to behave differently, since it is not linear.
The toy has one number per sample and a perfect denoiser, so the sizes of the changes do not transfer to pictures.
